questions.question: Explain the causes of slave resistance at the Cape.
questions.expected_answer: Loss of freedom and forced unpaid labour; harsh treatment and cruel punishment; families broken up by sales; denial of rights (no legal marriage, property, free movement or testimony); memories of freedom and home in Madagascar, Mozambique, India, Indonesia; new ideas of liberty from the French Revolution (1789), the Haitian Revolution (1791-1804) and the British abolition of the slave trade (1807).

questions.question: Describe the different forms of slave resistance at the Cape, with examples.
questions.expected_answer: Everyday resistance: working slowly, pretending illness, breaking tools, taking goods; preserving language, culture and faith (Islam, literacy); complaints to courts; individual violence; running away (drosters) to the mountains, ships, interior, Khoikhoi/San/Xhosa communities; maroon communities such as Cape Hangklip; open rebellion, e.g. the 1808 rebellion led by Louis of Mauritius with James Hooper and Abraham Kieviet - over 300 marched from the Swartland to Salt River.

questions.question: What were the effects of slave resistance?
questions.expected_answer: Individuals: whipping, branding, chains, imprisonment, execution (five hanged after 1808, including Louis). Colony: fear among owners, stricter controls on movement, passes, weapons and gatherings, patrols. Wider: showed that enslaved people never accepted slavery; alarmed the British; with resistance across the empire and abolitionists, built pressure leading to 1820s reforms (Protector of Slaves, marriage, self-purchase) and abolition in 1834; preserved culture and identity.
